properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECB mode is used in multiple crypto backend files for cipher operations. This is a serious cryptographic weakness as identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks, making it vulnerable to pattern analysis attacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Camellia cipher is used in multiple crypto backend files. While it's a quantum-resistant algorithm, it's not part of the NIST-approved set and doesn't provide the same level of standardization as AES-256-GCM.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Counter, CFB and OFB modes are used in crypto backend files. These modes by themselves don't provide authentication and are vulnerable to malleability unless a separate MAC is applied.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is used in multiple crypto backend files for key derivation purposes. This is a standard and acceptable practice for password-based key derivation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE2 and BLAKE3 hash functions are used in crypto backend files. These are quantum-safe algorithms, but they're not the primary concern for quantum vulnerability assessment which focuses on RSA, ECDH, DH key exchanges.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Argon2id is used in crypto backend files for password-based key derivation. This is a modern, secure algorithm that provides good resistance to both side-channel and time-memory trade-off attacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 hash functions are used in crypto backend files. These are quantum-safe algorithms, but not the primary concern for quantum vulnerability assessment which focuses on RSA, ECDH, DH key exchanges.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CCM/SIV modes are used in crypto backend files. These are authenticated encryption modes that provide both confidentiality and integrity, and are not quantum-vulnerable primitives.
